questions.question: With prefix[0] = 0 and prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + nums[i], what is the sum of nums[l..r] inclusive?
questions.explanation: prefix[r + 1] holds the sum of nums[0..r] and prefix[l] holds the sum of nums[0..l-1]; subtracting leaves nums[l..r].

questions.question: In the 'subarray sum equals k' solution, why is the map seeded with 0 → 1?
options: So subarrays that start at index 0 are counted
To make the map iterate in insertion order
questions.explanation: A subarray from index 0 to i has sum equal to the running sum itself, which requires an earlier prefix of 0, the empty prefix.

questions.question: When are prefix sums a poor choice for range-sum queries?
options: When values are updated frequently between queries
When the array contains negative numbers
When the array is larger than 1,000 elements
questions.explanation: Updating one element forces an O(n) rebuild of the prefix array. For dynamic data, Fenwick or segment trees are used instead.

questions.question: Using a difference array, how do you record 'add 10 to every element from index 2 to index 5'?
questions.explanation: The +10 starts at the left index and is cancelled just after the right index, so a prefix-sum pass adds 10 only to positions 2 through 5.
